42367-the-stones-of-paris-in-history-and.title: In History And Letters
42367-the-stones-of-paris-in-history-and.creator: Benjamin Ellis Martin
42367-the-stones-of-paris-in-history-and.description: A book by Benjamin Ellis Martin. In preceding chapters we have come upon the small beginnings of the Scholars' Quarter; we have had glimpses of the growth of the great mother University and of her progeny of out-lying colleges; and we have trodden, with their scholars and students, the slope of "the whole Latin Mountain," as it was named by Pantaléon, that nephew of Pope Urban IV., who extolled the learning he had acquired here.

65247-a-class-book-of-new-testament-hist.title: A Class Book Of New Testament History
65247-a-class-book-of-new-testament-hist.creator: Unknown

THE present Volume forms a sequel to the Author’s Class-Book of Old Testament History, continuing the Narrative from the point at which it there ends, and carrying it on to the close of St Paul’s second imprisonment at Rome.

arxiv-2012-07423.title: Twisted superfluid and supersolid phases of triplons in bilayer honeycomb magnets
arxiv-2012-07423.creator: Dhiman Bhowmick 1, Abhinava Chatterjee 1,2,∗, Prasanta K. Panigrahi 2, Pinaki Sengupta 1
arxiv-2012-07423.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Dhiman Bhowmick 1, Abhinava Chatterjee 1,2,∗, Prasanta K. Panigrahi 2, Pinaki Sengupta 1. We demonstrate that low-lying triplon excitations in a bilayer Heisenberg antiferromagnet provide a promising avenue to realise magnetic analogs of twisted superfluid and supersolid phases that were recently reported for two-component ultracold atomic condensate in an optical lattice.

arxiv-2105-11164.title: Chemical abundances in the nuclear region of nearby galaxies from the Palomar Survey 2021 Chemical abundances in the nuclear region of nearby galaxies from the Palomar Survey – 13
arxiv-2105-11164.creator: B. Pérez-Díaz, J. Masegosa, I. Márquez, E. Pérez-Montero
arxiv-2105-11164.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by B. Pérez-Díaz, J. Masegosa, I. Márquez, E. Pérez-Montero. We estimate chemical abundances and ionization parameters in the nuclear region of a sample of 143 galaxies from the Palomar Spectroscopic Survey, composed by Star-Forming Galaxies (87), Seyferts 2 (16) and LINERs (40) using the Hii-Chi-mistry code. We also study for each spectral type the correlation of the derived quantities with other different properties of the host galaxies, such as morphology, stellar mass, luminosity and mass of their Supermassive Black Holes.

arxiv-2212-04473.title: Diffusion Guided Domain Adaptation of Image Generators
arxiv-2212-04473.creator: Kunpeng Song 1, Ligong Han 1, Bingchen Liu 2, Dimitris Metaxas 1, Ahmed Elgammal 1, 3]
arxiv-2212-04473.description: Abstract Can a text-to-image diffusion model be used as a training objective for adapting a GAN generator to another domain? In this paper, we show that the classifier-free guidance can be leveraged as a critic and enable generators to distill knowledge from large-scale text-to-image diffusion models.

arxiv-2305-08533.title: Trustchain – Trustworthy Decentralised Public Key Infrastructure for Digital Credentials
arxiv-2305-08533.creator: Tim Hobson, Lydia France, Sam Greenbury, Luke Hare, Pamela Wochner
arxiv-2305-08533.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tim Hobson, Lydia France, Sam Greenbury, Luke Hare, Pamela Wochner. The sharing of public key information is central to the digital credential security model, but the existing Web PKI with its opaque Certification Authorities and synthetic attestations serves a very different purpose. We propose a new approach to decentralised public key infrastructure, designed for digital identity, in which connections between legal entities that are represented digitally correspond to genuine, pre-existing relationships between recognisable institutions.

arxiv-2407-06013.creator: Michail Fasoulakis †, Konstantinos Varsos ‡, Apostolos Traganitis §, † Department of Computer Science
arxiv-2407-06013.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Michail Fasoulakis †, Konstantinos Varsos ‡, Apostolos Traganitis §, † Department of Computer Science. By the seminal paper of Claude Shannon [ 10 ] , the computation of the capacity of a discrete memoryless channel has been considered as one of the most important and fundamental problems in Information Theory. Nearly 50 years ago, Arimoto and Blahut independently proposed identical algorithms to solve this problem in their seminal papers [ 1 , 2 ] .

arxiv-2411-02320.title: An Empirical Study on the Code Refactoring Capability of Large Language Models
arxiv-2411-02320.creator: Jonathan Cordeiro, Shayan Noei, Ying Zou
arxiv-2411-02320.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) aim to generate and understand human-like text by leveraging deep learning and natural language processing techniques. In software development, LLMs can enhance the coding experience through coding automation, reducing development time and improving code quality.

arxiv-2509-13489.title: Extended Abstract: Towards a Performance Comparison of Syntax and Type-Directed NbE
arxiv-2509-13489.creator: Chester J.F. Gould, William J. Bowman
arxiv-2509-13489.description: Abstract . A key part of any dependent type-checker is the method for checking whether two types are equal. A common claim is that syntax-directed equality is more performant, although type-directed equality is more expressive. However, this claim is difficult to make precise, since implementations choose only one or the other approach, making a direct comparison impossible.

pmc-10740488.title: Interhospital Spread of blaVIM-1- and blaCTX-M-15-Producing K. pneumoniae ST15 on an IncR Plasmid in Southern Spain
pmc-10740488.creator: Patricia Pérez-Palacios, Ana Gual-de-Torrella, Ines Portillo-Calderón, Esther Recacha-Villamor, Francisco Franco-Álvarez de Luna, Lorena Lopez-Cerero, Alvaro Pascual, Alessandra Piccirilli, Mariagrazia Perilli
pmc-10740488.description: In 2014–2015, the main CTX-M-15- and OXA-48-producing clone in our region was ST15. Recently, K. pneumoniae ST15 isolates co-producing VIM-1 and CTX-M-15 were detected in several hospitals. The aim was to study the emergence and acquisition of this carbapenemase. Between 2017 and 2019, four hospitals submitted twenty-nine VIM-1- and CTX-M-15-producing K. pneumoniae ST15 isolates to our laboratory.

pmc-11322287.title: Phytochemical screening, antioxidant, anti-diabetic, and anti-obesity activities, formulation, and characterization of a self-nanoemulsion system loaded with pomegranate (Punica granatum) seed oil
pmc-11322287.creator: Ahmad M. Eid, Linda Issa, Khalid Arar, Ahmad Abu-Zant, Mohammad Makhloof, Yazan Masarweh
pmc-11322287.description: Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a tree of the Punicaceae family that is widespread all over the world and has several types and therapeutic uses. The current study aimed to investigate the phytochemical compounds by GC analysis and carried out physical characterization of the pomegranate seed oil and its self-nanoemulsifying system. Then antioxidant, anti-diabetic, and anti-lipase activities were investigated for both.

pmc-11325633.title: Barriers and facilitators when implementing midwifery continuity of carer: a narrative analysis of the international literature
pmc-11325633.creator: Aimee Louise Middlemiss, Susan Channon, Julia Sanders, Sara Kenyon, Rebecca Milton, Tina Prendeville, Susan Barry, Heather Strange, Aled Jones
pmc-11325633.description: BackgroundMidwifery continuity of carer (MCoC) is a model of care in which the same midwife or small team of midwives supports women throughout pregnancy, birth and the postnatal period. The model has been prioritised by policy makers in a number of high-income countries, but widespread implementation and sustainability has proved challenging.

pmc-11506467.title: Effective Boundary Correction for Deterministic Lateral Displacement Microchannels to Improve Cell Separation: A Numerical and Experimental Study
pmc-11506467.creator: Shaghayegh Mirhosseini, Mohammadmahdi Eskandarisani, Aryanaz Faghih Nasiri, Fatemeh Khatami, Akram Mirzaei, Majid Badieirostami, Seyed Mohammad Kazem Aghamir, Mohammadreza Kolahdouz
pmc-11506467.description: Particle separation and sorting techniques based on microfluidics have found extensive applications and are increasingly gaining prominence. This research presents the design and fabrication of a microfluidic device for separating cells using deterministic lateral displacement (DLD), enabling accuracy and continuity while being size-based.

pmc-11546597.title: Evaluating Virtual Reality Patient Education in Cardiac Surgery: Impact on Preoperative Anxiety and Postoperative Patient Satisfaction
pmc-11546597.creator: Sulayman el Mathari, Lieke Kuitert, Noor Boulidam, Saadullah Shehadeh, Robert J M Klautz, Robert de Lind van Wijngaarden, Jolanda Kluin, Francesco Giallauria
pmc-11546597.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Preoperative anxiety in cardiac surgery patients can adversely affect mental well-being and postoperative outcomes. Virtual reality (VR) patient education has been proposed as a novel method to enhance patient education and potentially reduce preoperative anxiety. The VR Patient Journey Trial aimed to evaluate the impact of VR patient education on preoperative anxiety and patient satisfaction compared to traditional education methods. Methods: This randomized controlled trial included 121 patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

pmc-11642112.title: Dopamine: A New Player in the Pathogenesis of Diabetic Retinopathy?
pmc-11642112.creator: Marianthi Ntikoudi, Theofano Myrto Farmaki, Konstantinos Tziomalos
pmc-11642112.description: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness. The pathogenesis of diabetic retinopathy is multifactorial and incompletely understood. Accordingly, treatment options are limited. Recent data suggest that dopamine might play a role in the development and progression of DR.

pmc-12546446.title: Anti-CD38 and Regression of Chronic Active Antibody-Mediated Rejection After Kidney Transplantation - Myth or Reality?
pmc-12546446.creator: Marie Matignon, Philippe Grimbert, Anissa Moktefi, Caroline Pilon

pmc-12730416.title: Subtype-Independent Dysregulation of the Notch Signaling Pathway and Its miRNA Regulators in Breast Cancer
pmc-12730416.creator: Elżbieta Mitka-Krysiak, Katarzyna Król-Jatręga, Piotr Ossowski, Nikola Zmarzły, Krzysztof Bereza, Paweł Ordon, Wojciech Kulej, Tomasz Sirek, Agata Sirek, Kacper Boroń, Maciej Boroń, Dariusz Boroń, Beniamin Oskar Grabarek, Georgia Levidou
pmc-12730416.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: The Notch signaling pathway regulates cell fate, proliferation, and differentiation, and its dysregulation has been implicated in various cancers, including breast cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical post-transcriptional regulators that can modulate Notch pathway components. The aim of this study was to identify miRNAs that may potentially regulate the expression of Notch pathway-related genes across five molecular subtypes of breast cancer in Polish women.

pmc-12737062.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Analysis of Aquaporin Gene Family in Tea Plant (Camellia sinensis)
pmc-12737062.creator: Huiyi Wang, Jiaojiao Tuo, Huixin Shao, Shiyi Chen, Hongli Cao, Chuan Yue
pmc-12737062.description: Aquaporins (AQPs) facilitate transmembrane transport of water and small solutes, critically influencing plant growth, development, and stress adaptation. However, tea plant AQPs (CsAQPs) remain incompletely characterized genome-wide. In this study, 61 CsAQPs were identified from the tea plant genome and could be classified into five subfamilies.

pmc-12768725.title: OP24 Cost Effectiveness Of Monitoring Ocular Hypertension Based On A Risk Prediction Tool
pmc-12768725.creator: Hangjian Wu, Gus Gazzard, Anthony King, James Morgan, David Wright, David Crabb, Yemisi Takwoingi, Augusto Azuara-Blanco, Verity Watson, Rodolfo Hernández
pmc-12768725.description: IntroductionGlaucoma is a leading cause of blindness. Ocular hypertension (OHT) is a key risk factor modifiable by regular monitoring and treatment. Population aging leads to rapid rise of OHT patients, and thus overburdens the UK healthcare system, but innovative technology may provide a solution.

pmc-13375692.creator: Bhupendra Raj Giri, Jamie Erin Spahn, Rawidh Alsaidalani, Beatriz Behrend-Keim, Mohammed Bhia, Jailen Haley Doyle, Matthew Joseph Herpin, Rex Corbin Moore, Nila Sangeetha Murali, Arifenur Safak, Hugh David Charles Smyth

pmc-13459307.title: Embodied meaning in therapeutic discourse during cognitive-behavioral therapy for generalized anxiety disorder: an image schema analysis
pmc-13459307.creator: Fereshteh Mohamadpour, Mehrdad Askarian
pmc-13459307.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundImage schemas are simple mental structures that are formed from the body’s interaction with the physical environment. One of the leading theories in this area is the one proposed by Mark Johnson.

pmc-13521004.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals and validates lipid raft–associated biomarkers and functional networks in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-13521004.creator: Chun-Hsien Hsu, Amadou Wurry Jallow, Fatima Saleem, Thi Minh Chau Vu, Yung-Feng Lin
pmc-13521004.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) involves complex changes, including synaptic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and metabolic impairment, yet the role of lipid raft–associated gene networks in these processes remains unclear. In this study, we performed an integrative transcriptomic analysis using the GSE5281 dataset and validated the findings in an independent cohort (GSE33000).

pmc-13532031.title: Osteoarthritis Therapeutics: From Microenvironment Understanding to Regenerative Intervention—Current Advances and Future Perspectives
pmc-13532031.creator: Yongbiao Meng, Shenghua Wu, Quanchun Liu
pmc-13532031.description: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent, chronic degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage degeneration and impaired joint function. Its rising global incidence poses a significant health and socioeconomic burden. Traditional therapies primarily offer symptomatic relief but fail to halt disease progression and are associated with notable limitations.

pmc-13598589.title: Enhanced osteogenic potential of chitosan scaffolds loaded with Lawsonia inermis, hydroxyapatite particles, and dental pulp stem cells in rats
pmc-13598589.creator: Maryam Karandish, Golnaz Ziaei, Fatemeh Akbarizadeh, Negar Azarpira, Shahrokh Zare, Ahmad Vaez, Nader Tanideh
pmc-13598589.description: IntroductionMaxillary/alveolar bone reconstruction is vital for cleft and pre-prosthetic patients. Autogenous bone (iliac crest) is the gold standard for clefts due to its bone-forming ability. For large defects (trauma/tumor), the vascularized fibula flap is preferred for its strength and blood supply.MethodsThis study investigates the physicochemical and biological properties of chitosan (Cs)-based scaffolds.

pmc-13608105.title: Damage Evolution During Thread Rolling of TC16 Titanium Alloy Using Coupled Johnson-Cook Constitutive and Damage Models
pmc-13608105.creator: Jianxin Cao, Xin Song, Ning Han, Huiping Qi
pmc-13608105.description: In this work, a coupled Johnson-Cook (J-C) constitutive and damage modeling framework was established to investigate damage evolution during thread-rolling of TC16 titanium alloy. The J-C constitutive parameters were calibrated through tensile tests under different strain rates and temperatures, while the stress-triaxiality-dependent damage parameters were identified using specimens with different stress states.
